interactions.title: Callie asks Wellby to help Ander
lines: DM: So, so as you approach, um, Callie comes out, sort of senses you coming, and com— comes and sort of cuts you off a little bit and kind of pulls you off to the side, uh, to talk and says, uh, "Wellby, g— good to see you. It's, it's been a tough few days. Uh, my brother, he's... Well, he's not getting worse so much, but he's definitely not getting better.

DM: "And a couple days ago at the market he had one of his episodes, and... Well, m— my grandmother's very upset. She, you know, we've sold hardly anything. It's been a... It's been very bad. If there's, if you have any good news at all, I would love to hear it."
Wellby: Well, uh, uh, no, I don't. Um, uh, in a few days after the festival the town's gonna be moving west. Most people are evacuating for safety. Perhaps you'll have better luck there.
DM: "We'd heard some rumors. I, I didn't know what to think."
Wellby: [sighs] Yeah. They'll move on to Tokra.
Wellby: Is there anything else that you can tell me about Raven's Hold or the road between here and there? I'm going with my companions to investigate.
DM: Uh, the road, well, it's not a bad journey. Um, the road, the track is clear the entire way. Uh, there are a few, uh, good oases, good spots to get water. Um, you know, it's...

DM: In the past, it's always felt like the safest part of the journey. Like, you come through the mountains, and it's always a little dicey, but the, you know, last 10 days or so through Dunmar, uh, are relaxing and, you know. The, the plains up north are, are much more hospitable than the deserts to the south. It's not quite so dry. Um, can be quite pretty at times even. But now, I don't know, after what happened at Raven's Hold. Nothing chased us particularly. We didn't have any trouble on the road, but, you know, I've been hearing all sorts of rumors. I don't know if the same will hold in the future.

DM: Um, Raven's Hold itself is set a, a few miles off the track, uh, east. But it's pretty obvious. I mean, you can see it from the road. The, the mountains themselves form a sharp rise f— from the plains, and Raven's Hold is sat in a, in a valley. Uh, there's a, a wall across the valley, and you can see the, um, the outer wall and the, the keep, the fortress set up a little bit in the valley from the road. Um, it's never been a place that seemed very hospitable to explore. I think there's some dwarven caves there or something like that as well, uh, I've heard. Um, there...

DM: There is a, a small str— a river. Well, I shouldn't say a river, a stream that flows out, and it's, the gatehouse seems to, like it's fallen in. So it's, if you wade through the river, it's pretty easy to just get in that way. But I've never explored myself. It's always seemed a little bit too creepy for my taste.
Wellby: Is there any approach to it that isn't visible? Uh, I mean, presumably not, since it's built as a fortress, but there's no...
DM: None that I'm aware of.
Wellby: Hmm. Hmm. Do you know where the dwarven caves are? Worth finding out.
DM: No. I've just heard rumors.

DM: "If you're going there..." And she, like, sort of looks, you know, very much concerned. "If you find anything that might help Ander, please, I guess we're gonna be heading to Tokra with everybody else, but please t— you know, come, tell me, let us know, because I don't know how much longer he's gonna be able to live like this. We'd really appreciate it."
Wellby: We'll see you in Tokra, and if not Tokra, then beyond, Sangara.
DM: "We'll see you in Tokra." Is there anything else you'd like to try and learn from the halflings?

before: DM: Yep.

Kenzo: Kenzo wants to spend a little bit of time, um, talking about, uh, kind of the Lakan, um, occult, and then also understanding more, a little bit more about the history of what's going on with, um, the Shakun. DM: Right.
Kenzo: ... the, uh, the lay of the land there.

lines: Wellby: Uh, I don't think so. I mean, u— unless we can get anything more out of her brother that's not just rambling more of the same.

DM: Yep.

Seeker: And I keep thinking about this oddity of the temple somehow being older than the mesa. And so I'm just gonna look around the edges, the seams, the intersection points between the, the worked stone and the raw.

interactions.title: Seeker unbinds his illustrated booklet
lines: Seeker: So I have one non-obvious conclusion from all of this that is very indirect. I sit down next to this very strange wall at an intersection of the old and new areas, and I take from my pack the newly bound, um, uh, Legendary Staff of Kenzo, full of illustrations of different poses over the course of a few seconds. And I take it apart, unbinding it, and flip through it like a flip book. You can see almost, it's almost like an animation of Kenzo fighting, fighting, fighting. [clears throat] I take it all apart, lay them side by side in different arrangements, try to think about time.

before: DM: [laughs]
Seeker: Wow, that's amazing.
DM: It seems to be.
Seeker: And does it... Wow. And I have no idea what timescale this would have happened over.
DM: No, but you know the temple is supposed to be, you know, predates the Great War.
after: Seeker: And then I take out some maps, and put them side by side, and then start to make small copies of them, new ones, imagining landscapes changing. Stack them up and run my finger through them like a f— a flip book. And anyway, I'm imagining four-dimensional maps.
DM: Nothing happens.
Seeker: Oh, no, I'm not trying to cause any magic to happen.
DM: Okay, okay. You're just sort of interrogating your mind and trying to unders— wrap your arms around this.
Kenzo: He's developing a mental framework through which to, uh, analyze this phenomenon that he's observed.

interactions.title: Candrosa discusses northern religion and history
lines: DM: Yes. Okay, Kenzo, you wanted to talk to Candrosa?
DM: What do you wanna talk to him about? Or what do you want to ask him? He's, so he's, he's, uh, headed back to the temple, but you can, you, like, walk with him as he's heading back to the temple.

Kenzo: Okay. Sure. [clears throat] Candrosa, as we head north, [clears throat] well, first, I, I wish I had more, more time to spend here with you to learn more about the Shakun. Um, that was, as you know, this is my original purpose in coming. But, um, maybe we will have some time, uh, later. But, you know, as you know, the, these, these current events are, are, um, are perhaps gonna get the best of us.

Kenzo: But, um, as we venture north, um, can you share more about, about, um, any of the, the, the prevalence of any of the other gods or, or shrines or temples or other, um, you know, manifestations of the occult that we should either be aware for, aware of that may be there or may have even been contaminated or, or twisted in some way, um, based on your understanding of these events? Is there anything that you th— you think, you think we should know?

DM: Sort of pauses for a moment. I, I don't, I don't know of any, you know, monasteries or temples or any sort of hidden secrets to the north. That was, you know, back in our... I'm not an expert in our history, but from what I understand, much of the north was, was a war zone for much of the history of Dunmar. And, uh, you know, I think many of the, the people who were, lived and were garrisoned that far north were, uh, often, if not always, uh, you know, devotees of Aagir.
DM: Aagir is a... He is a, a... He is a necessary god, but perhaps not the most pleasant of gods.

DM: Fire and death are, are needed to have life and rebirth. The, the grasslands have to burn occasionally, or new grass won't grow. But, you know, the, the god of destruction is not one to pray to lightly. [coughs]
Kenzo: Does A— does Aagir... So Aagir is one of, like, it's Laka, Aagir, Shakun. Like, he's one of the—
Kenzo: ... I would know of who that is, that—
DM: ... he is one of the, like... So Jeevali, Laka, Aagir, one of the, like, Five Siblings in the, in the pantheon.
Kenzo: Got it. Got it. And that's what you see—
Seeker: That's the, the, the god whose temple we were in, in the other, in the first—
DM: That's... Exactly. That's the same god whose temple was in the fort—
DM: ... that we were in before.
Seeker: It all kind of makes sense. Like, it's the dominant religion. A fort is full of fighter warrior types. That's the one that they choose to worship.
Kenzo: ... Candrosa, are you saying that there, there, um, there are temples to Aagir in the north, or shrines to Aagir in the north?

DM: Well, I, I mean, that, that far north has not been settled since the Great War. There's good grazing land up there. The, the land, the, the land is not as dry. There's more water, but it's not been... I, I, I don't know who... I don't know, I don't know what's there. I, I—
DM: I... But I suspect that m— many of the people who, who spent their lives on the edge of civilization would have trusted to Aagir to keep them safe and destroy their enemies.
Kenzo: Do you know, do you know much about the history of Raven's Hold? Any, any, any story of its lore or any sense of its history?

DM: Uh. [sighs] Not really. I don't... It was a fort. I, I think it might have been a, a place where the dwarves traded or had some outpost. The, you know, the dwarves who used to... [laughs] Yes, he is.

DM: I, so I don't... I, I guess I don't... I, I'm not sure I can help you much. I, I would say, you know, my experience has been not of the history of our people, but the gods as they are now. And as we've discussed, that's been a trying experience in the past few months.

Kenzo: Is, is there somebody in the town that can shed more light on the history of Raven's Hold for us? I think, you know, it, it feels like it's, it's certainly a, a source of, of some, I don't know if evil's strong, too strong a word, but something is not right there. And I think before me and my companions, uh, um, face whatever's there, we, we best equip ourself with which, with as much knowledge as we can about the history and the, the lore of this place. Who, who might be able to tell us more?
DM: I, so Alesh is the o— I mean, this is not what he's saying, but r— you remember—
DM: ... Alesh is sort of the one who everybody's told you—
DM: ... is kind of the student of history around here, and she's planning to talk to you briefly before she—
DM: And so Candrosa says, "Yeah, I mean, A— Alesh is probably the one to talk to. I believe she wanted to say goodbye to you before she—"
DM: "... rode south at, at this evening. So perhaps she'll see you at the inn."

Kenzo: Okay. Okay. Candrosa, thank you, and, you know, we, we, we won't... We, we will still be here for, for, um— for a few days, um, obviously preparing and helping to fortify the temple. But if you think of anything else that we should know as we prepare for our journey, please, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Kenzo: And similarly, just from our connection and our, our, our similar studies, if you, if there's something that, if there's a training that you think I might benefit from as well, um, as, as we travel, please, please also let me know.
Kenzo: Okay. Um, [clears throat] all right.

lines: DM: So, um, that evening, um, Alesh rides over to, um, say goodbye to you. Um, she's traveling with two other Dunmari, one an older man, grizzled, gre— going gray hair who, who... So they, this is a quick meeting because they're heading this, they're leaving this evening before the festival because they wanna, uh—

DM: ... they're gonna c— try and cover a lot of ground heading south. Um, and this guy, uh, just watching him ride up, it al— you almost think you're watching some mythical creature like a centaur ride up. He seems like one with his horse. Um, and then another woman cloaked and hooded and kinda nondescript looking, but with a longbow and two quivers of arrows, um, slung on her horse. And Alesh sort of rides ahead of them and comes over to you and says...

DM: "Friends, we're leaving tonight and hope to cover 200 miles or more before we return. Should we, should we make a plan for, for when to meet or, uh, or how long for when to return to, to Karawa to regroup before we leave? I don't know how... We won't be able to communicate until we—"
DM: "... are back in the same place."
Kenzo: We, we were discussing exactly this, this question. How long do you need for your travel south to cover these 200 miles?

DM: Hmm. That's a good question. DM: But Jeevali wept for her people, crying tears that poured from the heavens, cleansing the land, purifying the soil, and creating rivers that flowed to the sea. As she cried, though, she put so much of her power and spirit into her tears that she began to fade away, diminished, and was gone. But the land sprung up in richness and life, and the grass grew, and the herds prospered.

DM: And for a year, the people prayed, singing her name every day, calling to her and begging for her r— to return. That first harvest in the new land was an incredibly bountiful one. The lambs and calves and foals were healthy and productive and survived. And as the winter rains fell gently on the land, the people prayed and chanted her name.

DM: And as the new life began to grow in the fertile soil, Jeevali herself appeared as this living tree with a spiral design growing up to the top, the power of the belief of the people summoning her back from the divine essence and restoring her form.

DM: And since then, the Festival of Rebirth has marked this event, the f— founding of Dunmar, the grace of Jeevali in saving the people, and the miracle of her restoration. And as she comes to the end of this tale, um, the people chant, and the sort of song goes through the crowds, um, and she lights the shrine on fire. And every year at the, at the evening of this festival, um, the people of Karawa burn this old shrine, and then in a procession in the new year, they... Or, uh, in the new day, uh, they bring pieces of the desert. They bring seeds and flowers and plants and create them into this shrine shape again. And then hopefully Jeevali will bless it, and it will grow and thrive.

DM: And of course, this year there's this undercurrent of fear running through the crowd, and worry, and, uh, uncertainty as everybody here is contemplating leaving in the next day or two, fleeing west into the... fleeing from what is not entirely clear. But whatever it is, it seems horrifying.

Pieces of it kind of drift off, almost like fireworks, floating in all directions, but mostly west. And as these embers drift to the west, a sort of sigh goes through the crowd as Suma says, "Jeevali has blessed us. Jeevali is going west, and we will follow her." And then offers a prayer in her name and, and a song, and, "In the, the morning, the day after the festival, we will gather, and we will leave, and Jeevali will be with us in this journey and keep us safe." And with that, the fires burn down to the ground, the ashes cool, and a gust of wind sort of swirls around the people, and this ash just kind of blows around everywhere and then [exhales] disperses.
DM: And with that, um, people kind of drift off. Uh, there's... Traditionally, people will fast until the feast at the, after the new shrine is blessed in the, in the midday.

Some resigned, some fearful, but all with a sort of sense of determination and, and relief that they can tell themselves they're going with the goddess's favor.

People have gathered all these, like, pieces of the desert and pieces of flowers and plants and everything that, that blooms and grows. So this procession winds through town, um, singing the praises of Jeevali, and it's, you know, it's normally a, like, sort of a, almost a, a celebratory at— atmosphere.
